name: Can a detached ADU be built while living in the main house?

mainEntity.name: Can homeowners stay in the main house during detached ADU construction without major disruption?
mainEntity.text: Can homeowners stay in the main house during detached ADU construction without major disruption?

acceptedAnswer.text: Living on-site during detached ADU construction is common, but comfort depends on how the project is managed. A detached build usually disrupts the main house less than a remodel because the work is outside the primary living area, yet it can still affect daily life through noise, dust, workers on site, blocked access, deliveries, and temporary utility shutoffs. On smaller lots, the construction zone can feel very close to the house, especially during excavation, concrete work, and framing. Homeowners should ask the contractor where staging, debris storage, and parking will happen before construction begins. A well-run job should include a dust-control plan, a communication routine, and a schedule for the loudest work. If privacy and quiet are priorities, it is worth discussing work hours, fencing, and site protection up front. Most discomfort comes from poor planning, not the ADU itself.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, many homeowners remain in the main house during detached ADU construction, but they should expect noise, dust, parking strain, material deliveries, and temporary utility interruptions. The level of disruption depends on site access and how close the new unit is to the primary home.
